summary:
Radar for 2026-10-31. Every candidate fits the GLP-1 focus.

**1. Biggest news: the retatrutide head-to-head is already peaking.** Lilly released TRANSCEND-T2D-2 on Oct 28: 19.5–20.9% weight loss on retatrutide versus 9.4% on semaglutide 2 mg at 80 weeks, and A1C down 2.2 versus 1.8 points. It is now more than 48 hours old, it's topline only (not peer-reviewed), and it covers type 2 diabetes. That rules it out for a Lane C long-form. Use it for one retatrutide "what's confirmed?" Short with a loop ending. Mainstream coverage is saturated (ABC, USA Today, NY Post, Reuters, STAT).

**2. No fresh randomized result qualifies for Lane C today.** The next likely trigger is ObesityWeek, Nov 14–17 in Washington DC, where Novo has announced new CagriSema and Wegovy-pill data. Watch it for a qualifying result within 48 hours.

**3. The best opportunity is still Lane A, in the playbook's order:**
- Stopping tirzepatide: SURMOUNT-4, plus the Metabolites regain review and the Oct 29 semaglutide persistence cohort.
- Protein on tirzepatide: refreshed by muscle-sparing pipeline hype that is animal data only.
- Hair loss.

**4. Two new Lane A hooks are opening, both seasonal:**
- Cold and flu season. Yahoo Health ran "On a GLP-1? Some cold meds can make side effects worse" on Oct 31. The search space is mostly telehealth SEO blogs, so competition is low.
- Thanksgiving. Search should peak Nov 18–27.

**5. Body-worry Shorts (honest uncertainty):**
- Older adults, frailty and falls. Signals: a JAMA news analysis on Oct 30, mixed falls data and the SELECT frailty post-hoc analysis.
- Pancreas and gallbladder: the scoping review plus a propensity-matched cohort.
- Mood and anxiety: a neuropsychiatric safety review plus a semaglutide panic-attack signal that mostly reflects reporting bias.

**6. Lower-priority emerging items:**
- ATTAIN-J orforglipron, published in Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol on Oct 30.
- Two new reviews on GLP-1 medicines and PCOS / insulin-resistant women.
- GLP-1 medicines and alcohol: a Medscape piece on what clinicians see, plus a tirzepatide PET trial protocol.

**7. Rejected:** the $69/$99 online GLP-1 programs, the Forbes "where to buy" and compounded-cost pieces, and gray-market angles. Cost, coverage, employer coverage and Medicare topics stay banned in long-form.

**Already covered recently, so not re-proposed:** food noise, fatigue, grocery cart and thyroid (all 10-31), Plateau, and Bones and Muscle.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335 randomized at week 36; +14.0% regain week 36→88 on placebo), refreshed by the Metabolites regain systematic review (Oct 9) and the new semaglutide early-trajectory/persistence cohort (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 29)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. Title: 'What Happens When You Stop Tirzepatide?'. First sentence answers it: on average, much of the weight came back within a year in SURMOUNT-4, while people who stayed on it kept losing. Then cover why (appetite biology, not willpower), what the regain review adds across drugs, and what habits trials and cohorts link to keeping results. Say 'don't stop, switch or change your medicines on your own' early and at the end.
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; boosted for 2–4 weeks by on/off coverage and New Year planning
candidates.why_now: It has appeared in 4+ snapshots at rising momentum (76→82). New regain and persistence papers came out this month, and CBC's on/off GLP-1 feature keeps the question mainstream. It's the next item in the playbook's Lane A order. The 'hunger after stopping' Reel scored 193 on Instagram.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of weight regain after stopping GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 drugs, Oct 9, 2026
Early treatment trajectory and long-term persistence on semaglutide for obesity, population cohort, Oct 29
Patterns of discontinuation, reinitiation and switching of semaglutide and tirzepatide

candidates.topic: Protein on tirzepatide: how much and why. Hooked on the muscle-sparing GLP-1 hype (Rivus animal data Oct 30, iBio primate data Oct 29), which is animal-only, against the human evidence (SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy, about 75% fat / 25% lean; J Clin Med Oct 15 cohort)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. Title: 'Protein on Tirzepatide: How Much and Why'. Open on 'you're barely hungry, so how do you hit protein?' and answer within 15 s. Use guideline-style ranges from major society or joint advisory statements, quoted exactly, with no tags on our own tips. Practical: protein first at each meal, easy foods when you're full fast, pair with strength training. Note that muscle-sparing add-on drugs are only in animals so far.
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; extra pull over the next 1–2 weeks from muscle-sparing pipeline news
candidates.why_now: Two muscle-sparing pipeline stories landed this week, and Food & Wine's protein trend piece is in earlier snapshots. Strength Training is our top Lane A earner, so a protein video sits right next to it in suggested traffic.

evidence.signal: Weight-loss size, fat mass and device-estimated muscle loss during obesity drug treatment, Oct 15
Rivus to show animal data on a muscle-sparing GLP-1 (Oct 30); iBio primate data (Oct 29)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and a cold or flu: what to know this season. Sick days, fluids, nausea stacking with cold medicines, and asking your pharmacist about decongestants (Yahoo Health, Oct 31)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form or Short. Title: 'Tirzepatide and a Cold or Flu: What to Know'. Answer first: tell your prescriber or pharmacist when you're sick, keep fluids up, and ask which cold medicines suit you. Explain why: the label's dehydration and kidney warnings when vomiting or diarrhea hit, and decongestants can raise blood pressure. Give no product or dosing instructions, and say not to skip, stop or change medicines on your own. Point to the flu shot positively, using CDC wording.

sick on glp-1 what to do
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–8 weeks (US/UK cold and flu season ramps up through December)
candidates.why_now: Mainstream pickup came today (Yahoo Health, Oct 31) as the seasonal respiratory cycle starts. Current results are mostly telehealth-seller SEO blogs (TrimRx and others), with no trusted explainer. The question is high-intent and long-tail.

evidence.signal: 'On a GLP-1? Some cold meds can make side effects worse. Here's what to take instead.' Oct 31, 2026
Shows search demand: 'Can I take NyQuil on Wegovy'

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common is it and what helps? 5.4% (119/2,183) vs 0.9% (22/2,221) (Gupta 2026); the label reports 7.1% of women vs 0.5% of men; refreshed by the Med Sci (Basel) skin side-effects review
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form (the L1 10-30 redo). First sentence gives the numbers. Say 'particularly associated with' and 'linked to rapid weight loss', and that no human studies show a direct effect on follicles. Then cover what helps: protein, iron and other checks with a clinician, and the usual timeline for shedding to settle.
keywords: does hair grow back after tirzepatide
candidates.why_now: Momentum is climbing across 4 snapshots (67→76). The Short scored 103 on YouTube and 142 on Instagram at day 2. It's next in the Lane A list, and the redo is still pending.

evidence.signal: Systematic review of skin side effects with semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide, Oct 9, 2026

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg in type 2 diabetes (TRANSCEND-T2D-2, Phase 3 topline, Oct 28): weight −19.5% (9 mg) and −20.9% (12 mg) vs −9.4%; A1C −2.2 vs −1.8 points at 80 weeks (baseline A1C 8.3%, BMI 36.8)
candidates.angle: 13:00 retatrutide Short with a 'what's confirmed?' frame and a loop ending. It's a head-to-head in people with type 2 diabetes on metformin, topline and not yet peer-reviewed, and retatrutide is not approved anywhere. Don't cover it as a long-form: it's more than 48 h old and coverage is saturated.
candidates.why_now: 20+ outlets have covered it since Oct 28 (Reuters, STAT, ABC, USA Today, NY Post, Medscape on Oct 30). Retatrutide Shorts with new Phase 3 data are our proven peaks (268, 205).

evidence.signal: Full topline numbers: A1C and weight at 80 weeks
Head-to-head trial coverage, Oct 28

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and semaglutide after 65: frailty, falls and muscle. JAMA news analysis 'Are GLP-1 drugs safe in people with frailty?' (Oct 30); Osteoporosis Int: semaglutide/tirzepatide linked to about 34% fewer falls vs DPP-4 inhibitors in older adults with T2D; FAERS falls signal; SELECT frailty post hoc
candidates.angle: 08:00 body-worry Short with honest uncertainty: 'Does tirzepatide raise fall risk after 65? The evidence points both ways.' Observational data are 'linked to' fewer falls; adverse-event reports can't show cause. Close on what helps: protein, strength and balance training, and blood-pressure checks with a clinician. Could become a future Lane A long-form ('Tirzepatide After 65').
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–3 weeks (Medicare Bridge is pushing older-adult uptake)
candidates.why_now: The JAMA analysis was published yesterday and WorldHealth.net ran a falls-after-65 piece today. Medicare GLP-1 uptake is surging in Lilly's Q3 news, so older viewers are arriving. The bones Short got 241.

evidence.signal: 'Analysis Asks: Are GLP-1 Drugs Safe in People With Frailty?' Oct 30, 2026
Semaglutide and tirzepatide linked to about 34% fewer falls and about 51% fewer femoral fractures vs DPP-4 inhibitors (observational, T2D, older adults)
SELECT frailty post hoc: semaglutide's cardiovascular benefit held with frailty

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: protein first, smaller plates, eating slowly and easing fullness and nausea at holiday meals
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form scheduled for about Nov 15–20: 'Thanksgiving on Tirzepatide: How to Enjoy the Meal'. A 'you' scenario at the table, a plate-building walkthrough, alcohol and rich food stacking nausea, and no restriction or 'skip the meal' messaging. Shorts follow in Thanksgiving week.

Keep each study at its own scope (class vs drug). Add a supportive line about talking to a clinician if mood changes, with no scare framing.
